questions.q: How does the narrator describe Claremont?
choices: The garbage-heap of the proud city
questions.explain: Sophiatown, Western Native Township and Claremont lie together; Kumalo is shocked by Claremont's shabbiness, dirt and crowding.

questions.q: What nickname do John Kumalo and his friends give the Bantu Press?
questions.explain: They think it moderate and that it 'does not say all that could be said.'

questions.q: Who is the woman Msimangu points out as 'one of the queens'?
choices: A liquor seller said to be one of the richest of their people in Johannesburg
questions.explain: The 'queens' are the illicit liquor sellers of Claremont.

questions.q: Why are many of the children in the streets not at school?
choices: Some do not care and some parents do not care, but many because the schools are full
They are all working in the mines
questions.explain: Overcrowded, insufficient schools are part of the picture of the broken city.

questions.q: At which address does Kumalo find Gertrude?
questions.explain: Msimangu waits next door at number thirteen while Kumalo goes in alone.

questions.q: What does Kumalo hear from inside the house before Gertrude opens the door?
choices: Laughter 'of which one is afraid' — a woman's voice and men's voices
questions.explain: Chairs are moved and things taken away before she comes to the door; there is fear in her eyes.

questions.q: What reason does Gertrude give for never writing to her family?
choices: She could not read or write
She had no money for a stamp
questions.explain: Kumalo presses her — 'Not two pennies for a stamp?' — and she does not answer.

questions.q: What does Gertrude say about the child when Kumalo asks where it is?
choices: She does not know — it must be fetched
questions.explain: That she is 'a liquor seller, a prostitute, with a child and you do not know where it is' is the shame Kumalo throws at her.

questions.q: What finally moves Kumalo from anger to gentleness with Gertrude?
choices: She weeps on the floor and says she wants to leave Johannesburg — 'I am a bad woman, my brother'
questions.explain: His 'deep gentleness returns'; he lifts her up, says 'God forgives us... Let us pray,' and they are reconciled.

questions.q: Who does Gertrude say will know where to find Absalom?
choices: The son of their brother John, who was often with Absalom
questions.explain: 'The son of our brother John and your son were often together. He will know.'
